sites.residue_label: extracellular beta-chain linker (post-furin cleavage site to pre-TM, residues ~763-957)
sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Insulin binding and internalization of FITC-labeled insulin confirmed (surface_and_function); ERK activation in a temporal pattern similar to endogenous receptors confirmed; AKT and ERK signaling also confirmed in C2C12 myoblasts (L7). Full surface_and_function validation.
sites.rationale: L1-L4 (PMC4837300) and L6-L8 (PMC12963976) all report full-length INSR constructs with an interdomain fluorescent-protein or SNAP-tag insertion placed between the furin-like cleavage region (RKRR at positions 759-762) and the transmembrane domain (958-978), placing the tag within the extracellular beta-chain linker (residues 763-957). No specific residue number is given in any of these clips, so the site is region-level. Python confirmed the RKRR furin motif at positions 759-762 and the TM boundary at 958, giving a 195-residue extracellular window. Functional signaling (ERK, AKT) and insulin binding were confirmed in multiple cell types, making this the highest-validated site in the ledger. Full-length InsRA and InsRB constructs with pH-resistant fluorescent proteins (TagGFP2, TagRFP, TagBFP) inserted into the extracellular domain between the furin-like cleavage region and the transmembrane domain, expressed in cultured beta-cells. The paper explicitly avoids known functional domains. No single residue number is given; the insertion is described by flanking landmarks (furin-like region and TM domain). The extracellular beta-chain spans residues 763-957 (RKRR furin site at 759-762, TM at 958-978).

sources.claim: To track the route of insulin receptors in living cells, we employed a novel tagging strategy whereby pH-resistant fluorescent proteins were placed at the extracellular domain of the insulin receptor in between the furin-like region and the transmembrane domain, avoiding the interruption of known functional domains [21] ( Figure 1 D).

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed (L12: 'surface display experiments'); EV transport experiments performed with Strep-tag II construct (L13). No explicit functional signaling assay reported in these clips for the tagged constructs.
sites.rationale: L12 and L13 both report N-terminal epitope tags (HA/FLAG and Strep-tag II, respectively) on full-length InsR, with surface display confirmed. The only possible extracellular N-terminal junction for a full-length receptor with SP 1-27 is after residue 27 (insert_after_residue=27), placing the tag at the mature N-terminus (residue 28 = H). Python verified G at position 27 and H at position 28, consistent with the canonical sequence. A tag placed upstream of residue 27 would be within the signal peptide and cleaved off, so insert_after_residue=27 is the only valid interpretation. No functional assay is reported in these clips. L12 (PMC12167996) reports full-length InsR expression plasmids with N-terminal HA and FLAG epitopes used in surface display experiments. L13 (PMC12167996) reports a Strep-tag II epitope followed by a Gly-Ser linker and HRV 3C site added to the N-terminus of full-length InsR. Neither clip names a residue number; the junction is derived from the signal peptide landmark (SP 1-27, mature N-terminus at residue 28). Python confirmed residue 27 = G (last SP residue) and residue 28 = H (first mature residue). The tag is placed after residue 27 (after SP cleavage) so it is displayed on the extracellular face.

sources.claim: Expression plasmids directing expression of full-length InsR and EGFR with and without N-terminal HA and FLAG epitopes are described elsewhere ( 70 ), pcDNA HA-NIS was a gift from Nancy Carrasco (Vanderbilt University, TN).

literature_notes: L5 (SNAP-tagged INSR from lentiviral vector) does not specify the position of the SNAP-tag; L6 contrasts 'inter-domain-tagged INSR' with 'terminal fusion proteins', suggesting the SNAP-tag in L5 may be a terminal fusion, but neither the terminus nor the residue is named, so it cannot be independently pinned as a surface site and is subsumed under the interdomain site (L1/L6). L9-L11 report a C-terminal myc tag used to discriminate exogenous from endogenous INSR in CHO cells; the C-terminus (residue 1382) is intracellular (topology 979-1382), so this is recorded in other_positions. The interdomain site (Site 1) has no pinned residue because none of the ledger lines for this region name a specific junction; the region spans ~195 residues (763-957) of the extracellular beta-chain. The N-terminal site (Site 2) is topology-derived: the paper says 'N-terminal' on full-length InsR, and the SP landmark (1-27) uniquely determines insert_after_residue=27.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal myc tag used to discriminate exogenous human INSR mutants from endogenous INSR in CHO Flp-In cells; residue 1382 is within the intracellular kinase domain (topology 979-1382), not on the extracellular surface.
